subject: Engelska 5
title: Vocabulary: collocations, phrasal verbs and word formation
sourceSummary: Do or make, common phrasal verbs, and how to build new words with prefixes and suffixes — what lifts your vocabulary from a pass to something nuanced.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct verb: "You need to ___ a decision before Friday."
questions.opener: The Swedish phrase "ta ett beslut" won't help you here.
questions.explanation: In English it's "make a decision". The Swedish "ta ett beslut" (literally "take a decision") often leads to the mistake "take a decision".

questions.prompt: Choose the correct verb: "I have to ___ my homework before dinner."
questions.opener: Tasks and chores take one verb, results and creations take another.
questions.explanation: "Do homework" — "do" is used for tasks, work and chores. "Make" is used when something is created or comes into being: make a cake, make a mistake.

questions.prompt: What does "put off" mean in: "They had to put off the meeting until next week"?
questions.opener: What happens to the meeting — is it cancelled, or moved?
questions.explanation: "Put off" means to postpone to a later time. To cancel completely is "call off" or "cancel".

questions.prompt: Choose the phrasal verb that fits: "Could you ___ my cat while I'm away?"
questions.opener: Which expression means to take care of someone or something?
questions.explanation: "Look after" = take care of. "Look for" = search for, "look up" = check a reference, "look into" = investigate.

questions.opener: Not all negations use the same prefix.
questions.explanation: The prefix "im-" is used before words starting with m and p: impossible, impatient, immature. "Un-" is the most common prefix generally (unhappy), but doesn't work here.

questions.prompt: Which noun is formed from the verb "develop"?
questions.opener: Which suffix turns a verb into a noun here?
questions.explanation: The suffix "-ment" forms nouns from certain verbs: develop → development, agree → agreement, improve → improvement.

questions.prompt: Correct the four collocation errors: "I made my homework, then I took a decision to make a break and take a photo of the sunset. It made me a lot of good."
questions.opener: Three of the mistakes are about do/make/take — and one expression is completely wrongly formed.
questions.answer: I did my homework, then I made a decision to take a break and take a photo of the sunset. It did me a lot of good.
steps: "made my homework" → "did my homework". Tasks and chores take "do".
"took a decision" → "made a decision". In English, decisions are "made".
"make a break" → "take a break". A break, a shower and a bus are "taken" in English.
"It made me a lot of good" → "It did me a lot of good". A fixed expression with "do". Note that "take a photo" in the original was already correct.

questions.prompt: When do you use "do" and when do you use "make"?
questions.opener: A rule of thumb plus the fixed expressions you need to know by heart.
questions.answer: Do: tasks, work, chores and unspecified activities — do homework, do the dishes, do research, do business, do someone a favour, do good. Make: when something is created or comes into being — make a decision, make a mistake, make progress, make an effort, make money, make friends, make noise. Rule of thumb: "do" for the activity, "make" for the result.
